Specialisation

Fintech Product
Design.

Financial products have one design constraint above all others: people have to trust them with their money. That changes everything — information hierarchy, feedback states, error handling, the weight of a destructive action. In fintech, good design is product reliability made visible.

Background

As Design Lead at Checkoff Finance for 3+ years, I've owned the full product design function — from early research and wireframes through to shipped design systems and front-end implementation. That experience runs alongside two other fintech product builds: Bankvole (consumer mobile banking) and Dedukt (B2B loan management).

Each product taught a different dimension of fintech design: consumer trust at the individual transaction level, institutional complexity in B2B loan workflows, and the operational demands of a live, regulated product over years — not sprints.

Focus areas

Design that earns
trust at every state.

Reducing cognitive load on high-stakes actions

Transfers, loan applications, payment confirmations — these actions carry real consequence. Clear information hierarchy, deliberate motion, and unambiguous feedback states keep users in control.

Designing for trust

Trust in a financial product is earned through consistency, clarity, and zero tolerance for ambiguity. Every state — loading, success, error, empty — is a trust signal.

Scalable design systems across mobile and web

Fintech products span mobile apps, web dashboards, and internal tools. Design systems built once, extended everywhere — no one-off screens.

Compliance-aware UI that still feels human

Regulatory requirements and good UX are not opposites. Compliance constraints become design constraints — the work is making them invisible to the user.
